answer:
Use the prebuilt `FunctionAgent` from `llama_index.core.agent.workflow`, passing it an LLM and a list of tools. The agent guide shows this import: "from llama_index.core.agent.workflow import FunctionAgent" [llama_index/docs/src/content/docs/framework/module_guides/deploying/agents/index.md]. It also builds the agent from a plain Python function: "agent = FunctionAgent(" [llama_index/docs/src/content/docs/framework/module_guides/deploying/agents/index.md]. The example passes `tools=[multiply]` and `llm=OpenAI(model="gpt-4o-mini")`.

Tool descriptions matter, because the model picks tools partly from their names and descriptions: "the tool selected (and the arguments written for that tool) rely strongly on the **tool name** and **description**" [llama_index/docs/src/content/docs/framework/module_guides/deploying/agents/tools.md]. In the example, the function's docstring serves as the description: "Useful for multiplying two numbers." [llama_index/docs/src/content/docs/framework/module_guides/deploying/agents/index.md]

If you need custom control over the steps, the docs point to Workflows: "LlamaIndex Workflows allow you to build very custom, agentic workflows through a core event-driven orchestration foundation." [llama_index/docs/src/content/docs/framework/use_cases/agents.md]. They also list a "Building a ReAct agent workflow" example there.

I only have these excerpts, which are truncated, so I can't confirm the full current API, parameters, or version-specific details. Check the linked tools and agent pages for those.
